```{python}
#| include: false
import calendar as pycal

import _common as c

cal = c.calendar().set_index("date")
ev = c.events()
```

::: {.tagline}
Every day of the 2026–27 Penn State year, shaded by how busy State College is expected to be.
:::

## The year at a glance

```{python}
#| output: asis
legend = " ".join(
    f'<span style="margin-right:1em"><span class="crowd-swatch crowd-{k}"></span>{k} {v}</span>'
    for k, v in c.CROWD_LABELS.items()
)
known = set(cal.index.strftime("%Y-%m-%d"))
months = []
for year, month in [(2026, m) for m in range(8, 13)] + [(2027, m) for m in range(1, 9)]:
    weeks = pycal.Calendar(firstweekday=6).monthdatescalendar(year, month)
    rows = []
    for week in weeks:
        cells = []
        for d in week:
            key = str(d)
            if d.month != month or key not in known:
                cells.append("<td></td>")
                continue
            row = cal.loc[key]
            tip = f"{d:%a %b %-d}: {row['crowd_label']}. {row['crowd_reason']}"
            if isinstance(row["events"], str):
                tip += f" ({row['events']})"
            classes = f"crowd-{row['expected_crowd']}" + (" event" if row["is_home_game"] else "")
            cells.append(f'<td class="{classes}" title="{tip}">{d.day}</td>')
        rows.append("<tr>" + "".join(cells) + "</tr>")
    head = "".join(f"<th>{d}</th>" for d in "SMTWTFS")
    months.append(
        f'<div class="month"><table><caption>{pycal.month_name[month]} {year}</caption>'
        f"<thead><tr>{head}</tr></thead><tbody>{''.join(rows)}</tbody></table></div>"
    )
print(c.raw(f'<p>{legend}</p><div class="month-grid">{"".join(months)}</div>'
            '<p style="font-size:.85rem;color:#54595d">Home football games are underlined. Hover over a day for details.</p>'))
```

## How the crowd level is set

Each day starts from the level for its part of the academic year. Big events can raise it but never lower it.

```{python}
#| output: asis
import pandas as pd
rules = pd.DataFrame([
    ["1", "Very quiet", "Thanksgiving, winter and spring breaks"],
    ["2", "Quiet", "Summer"],
    ["3", "Normal", "Regular semester days and finals"],
    ["4", "Busy", "Move-in, fall commencement, THON, the Friday before a home game"],
    ["5", "Packed", "Home football games, spring commencement, Arts Fest"],
], columns=["Level", "Label", "When"])
rules["Level"] = [f'<span class="crowd-swatch crowd-{k}"></span>{k}' for k in rules["Level"]]
print(c.html_table(rules))
```

These are stated assumptions, not measurements. Testing them would mean collecting restaurant data repeatedly through a semester and comparing game weeks with breaks.

## Key dates

```{python}
#| output: asis
tbl = ev.copy()
def when(s, e):
    if s == e:
        return f"{s:%a, %b %-d, %Y}"
    if s.year == e.year:
        return f"{s:%b %-d} – {e:%b %-d, %Y}"
    return f"{s:%b %-d, %Y} – {e:%b %-d, %Y}"
tbl["Date"] = [when(s, e) for s, e in zip(tbl["start_date"], tbl["end_date"])]
tbl["Event"] = tbl["event_name"]
tbl["Crowd"] = [f'<span class="crowd-swatch crowd-{k}"></span>{c.CROWD_LABELS[k]}' for k in tbl["expected_crowd"]]
tbl["Notes"] = tbl["notes"].fillna("")
tbl["Source"] = [f'<a href="{u}">{u.split("/")[2].replace("www.", "")}</a>' for u in tbl["source_url"]]
print(c.html_table(tbl[["Date", "Event", "Crowd", "Notes", "Source"]]))
```

Dates were checked against official Penn State sources in October 2026. The 2027 Blue-White Game is not included because its date had not been announced.
